reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an EasyBlock investment in StrongBlock-related nodes starting at $10, involving crypto conversion and bridging, share purchases, stated monthly returns, and an unusually high compounded APY. It also guides viewers through claiming rewards with a connected wallet, presenting a share-to-node-to-reward flow rather than a purely informational discussion. Although it includes a cautionary disclaimer, a stated fee, a displayed developer identity, and a stated lack of StrongBlock affiliation, the video still solicits crypto investment participation with high-return claims.

citations.quote: easyblock kindly reached out and this is a promotional video
You can buy shares at $10 each. And start earning 30% monthly returns in terms of STRONG by owning parts of STRONGblock nodes. By compounding your earnings, you can get up to 3,778% APY.
I'm not a financial advisor. Always do your own research. And be very careful. About what you invest in.
In order to claim your reward you need to visit easeblog.finance and click the claim rewards button, your reward will then be transferred to your connected wallet.

opening.argument: Judge the return figures as investment commentary, not a promise that every viewer will earn them. The speaker calls this a promotional video, so the commercial relationship is disclosed. He also makes the decision conditional on individual research and explicitly warns viewers to be careful about investing. Those qualifications matter when interpreting an enthusiastic discussion of potential returns.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the video states striking returns, but quoting a projected APY does not establish that the speaker guarantees it or conceals the promotion. The connected-wallet passage explains how a participant would claim a reward; it does not show a viewer receiving one. The explicit caution and conditional recommendation should count when assessing the video's overall message.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The caveats do not undo the solicitation. The video tells viewers they can buy shares and start earning monthly returns, gives an exceptionally high compounded APY, and describes a route to claim rewards through a connected wallet. Disclosure that the video is promotional clarifies its purpose; it does not turn the investment pitch into neutral market analysis.

opening.argument: Much of this is an operational walkthrough: the speaker explains why a smaller share exists, how accumulated contributions fund nodes, why gas costs affect reward timing, and where a user would claim rewards. He also points viewers to the developer's contact and code-related accounts. A careful judge can read the return figures as claims being examined within a technology demonstration, rather than proof that the speaker has verified an outcome for viewers.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's claim that this is not 'purely informational' sets too narrow a test. Explaining a buy-share-to-node workflow and a claim button is exactly what an operational demonstration would cover. The cited claim instruction describes a proposed process, not evidence that returns were paid to a viewer. Nor does the displayed purchase interface alone establish that the speaker completed a purchase.

citations.quote: In order to claim your reward you need to visit easeblog.finance and click the claim rewards button, your reward will then be transferred to your connected wallet.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The workflow is instructional precisely about joining the promoted investment: shares are bought, their proceeds fund nodes, and node revenue is described as distributed to users. The speaker couples that walkthrough with specific monthly and compounded return claims. Showing the mechanism without proving a completed payout does not make the invitation educational in its primary effect.

This revenue will be bridged back to phantom and distributed to users in USDC.
And start earning 30% monthly returns in terms of STRONG by owning parts of STRONGblock nodes. By compounding your earnings, you can get up to 3,778% APY.

opening.argument: This can be understood as promotion of a disclosed share-purchase service, without treating its advertised performance as verified. The terms include a minimum share price, a stated fee taken from rewards, and an express statement that the service is not affiliated with StrongBlock. The cited material describes buying shares and claiming rewards through a connected wallet; it does not, by itself, establish credential theft or a downline recruitment scheme. Those distinctions matter before calling the service fraudulent.

citations.quote: Easy Block has a minimum investment of around 10 dollars per share and a minimum gas fees.
Only a 10% fee is taken from StrongBlock rewards for development and marketing purposes
currently easy block has no affiliation with strong block
your reward will then be transferred to your connected wallet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution establishes that this is an investment promotion, but that alone does not establish the additional mechanisms it implies. The description identifies what purchasers receive as shares used to fund nodes, discloses a reward-based fee, and expressly disclaims StrongBlock affiliation. The claim-button instruction is not a request in the cited passage to disclose a password or recovery phrase. High advertised returns warrant skepticism, but they do not resolve those narrower questions.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Credential theft and recruitment are not necessary to identify the concern here. The purchase price is investment capital pooled to acquire nodes, not payment for an ordinary retail product. The video promotes recurring returns from those nodes, including 30% monthly and a compounded APY of up to 3,778%. Disclosing a fee and lack of affiliation does not change the promoted share-to-node-to-return proposition.
